patch.value: History-derived defect recurrence gate: turn resolved incident patterns into targeted local and hosted CI protections

The immutable tracker contains repeated defect families—extension alias contract loss, path normalization mismatches, history-cache invalidation regressions, Windows process and lock behavior, CLI liveness, release boundary mismatches, and gates that pass fixtures but fail real systems. Existing tests address individual instances, but no canonical service folds historical issues, resolutions, files, tests, error codes, relationships, and recurrence links into a versioned risk model that selects or requires the relevant checks for a new change. Build this as an SDK policy primitive used identically by local pre-push gates and GitHub Actions. Deterministic rules provide the blocking core; optional semantic clustering may propose families but cannot silently become a blocker.

A public SDK recurrence analyzer incrementally folds terminal issues, resolution evidence, linked files and tests, error codes, affected versions, and typed recurrence or supersedes edges into versioned defect families; Every family records canonical owner, trigger signals, required local checks, required hosted checks, negative control, escape budget, false-positive budget, and links to the historical items that justify it; A change-risk command and SDK call accept a commit, file set, package, or pm item and return a bounded explainable receipt naming selected families, evidence paths, required gates, omissions, and token and latency cost; Local pre-push and GitHub Actions consume the same generated policy artifact and fail on drift between their selected checks; hosted CI may add environment-only checks but cannot omit local deterministic checks; The initial backfill covers extension alias contracts, path and slug normalization, history projection invalidation, cross-platform process or lock behavior, CLI liveness, release and registry boundaries, and self-generated fixture blind spots; A closed defect cannot satisfy recurrence governance without a linked regression test, a deterministic non-test gate, or an explicit reviewed waiver with expiry; Optional semantic clustering only proposes families with evidence and confidence; deterministic identifiers, paths, test links, error codes, and typed edges control blocking behavior; The index is cursorable, resumable, merge-safe, and benchmarked on million-item multi-decade histories; incremental change analysis does not scan or serialize the full corpus; Mutation and policy changes append hash-chained history events so any recurrence model version and CI decision can be reconstructed later
Make every resolved defect teach local and hosted CI which failure class must never escape again
Historical context becomes an executable quality asset instead of a passive archive
Reduces recurring regressions while keeping fast local feedback targeted, explainable, and consistent with hosted enforcement
Each changed surface receives a bounded, evidence-linked recurrence risk receipt and the exact deterministic gates required by prior incidents
All-status review found repeated families with strong historical evidence but no portfolio owner that converts those relationships into change-aware CI selection

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text:
Recurrence census measured 2026-08-07 over all 2,007 terminal items and their 634 terminal Issues. This is offered as the concrete backfill input the acceptance criteria ask for: the families below are derived from the record rather than proposed from intuition, and each is stated with the evidence that would let a family be defined and a gate be chosen.

## Recurrence by source file — distinct terminal items that linked each file

| items | file |
|---|---|
| 247 | src/cli/main.ts |
| 147 | src/sdk/cli-contracts.ts |
| 110 | src/cli/commands/completion.ts |
| 105 | src/sdk/index.ts |
| 91 | src/cli/commands/create.ts |
| 76 | src/cli/commands/update.ts |
| 75 | src/core/extensions/loader.ts |
| 67 | src/cli/help-content.ts |
| 65 | src/mcp/server.ts |
| 65 | src/sdk/runtime.ts |

The distribution is the finding, not the ranking. Twelve percent of every closed and canceled item in this tracker touched one file. The top five are, almost exactly, the sites the contributor guidance enumerates as the mandatory replication set when a command is added or changed: the command barrel and entrypoint, the contract table, completions, the SDK surface, and the create path. The recurrence hot spots are therefore not risky code — they are the places a single logical change must be written more than once, and the recurring defect is a change applied at some sites and not all.

That reframes the family. It is not "main.ts is fragile". It is **multi-site wiring incompleteness**, its trigger signal is a diff that touches a strict subset of a declared replication set, and its gate is deterministic and local: derive the replication set from the contract table rather than from prose, and fail a change that leaves it partially written. Ruling O applies directly — the replication set is currently a checklist in a markdown file, which is enforcement by prose. The single-source-of-surface-tiering work is the structural fix and should be recorded as this family's canonical owner rather than a related item.

A second, compounding observation: the highest-recurrence file in the project is also the one nearest its size gate, at 99 percent of the 3,400-line cap. Recurrence density and cap proximity are being tracked by two unrelated items and neither reads the other's number. A file that is both the most-changed and the least-extensible in the corpus is the highest-value decomposition target the record can identify, and the recurrence index should expose that join.

## Recurrence by defect family — terminal Issues matching each title signature

| issues | family |
|---|---|
| 125 | flag and option contract, unknown-option recovery |
| 94 | extension and package install, activation |
| 77 | lock, concurrency, race, stale state |
| 72 | release, publish, registry boundary |
| 62 | output shape, projection, token cost |
| 46 | schema, type, status customization |
| 45 | history, hash chain, drift, restore |
| 43 | graph and dependency edge semantics |
| 42 | search, index, vector staleness |
| 35 | recovery and refusal message quality |
| 28 | Windows and cross-platform path or process |
| 18 | test-harness determinism and flake |

Signatures overlap and 191 terminal issues match none, so these are lower bounds and the residual is large enough that clustering must be evidence-driven rather than keyword-driven in the real implementation. Two families are worth calling out against the backfill list already recorded on this item.

The flag and option contract family is the largest at 125 and is not named in the current backfill scope. It is also the family with the most deterministic available gate, because the contract table already enumerates every flag and the conformance work already proposes a lexicon; a family here would mostly be wiring an existing contract into a blocking check rather than inventing a detector.

The concurrency family at 77 is the one where a local deterministic gate is genuinely unavailable, which is why the fault-and-concurrency simulation harness is its correct required check rather than a static rule. Recording it that way matters: the family model should be able to say that a family's required check is a seeded simulation, not only a lint or a test, or the model will under-cover exactly the defects that cost the most.

## Suggested first families, in the order the evidence supports

Multi-site wiring incompleteness — largest measured recurrence, deterministic gate, contract-derived trigger, and it subsumes part of the flag-contract family.
Flag and option contract divergence — largest issue family, existing contract to gate against.
Release and registry boundary — 72 issues and the only family whose escapes are visible to users of the published artifact rather than to contributors.
Concurrency and stale state — smaller, but the family whose required check must be a simulation, which is the modelling capability this item should prove early rather than late.

value.text: Defect-recurrence CI design. Mine closed incidents and fixes into normalized failure signatures keyed by violated contract, root cause, affected surface, triggering input, missing observation, and the earliest gate that could have stopped escape. Cluster only after preserving canonical incident identities; every promoted pattern creates or links one minimal negative control and one positive control, with the test linked back by verifies and discovered_from edges. Route fast deterministic controls to author-time or pre-push verification, broader property and compatibility matrices to hosted CI, and production-only signals to scheduled or release gates. Distinguish product regressions from infrastructure failures and flakes with rerun and timing evidence; never turn cancellation, silence, or rate limiting into approval. Measure recurrence rate, escaped-defect rate, time-to-detection, false-positive burden, flake rate, and coverage of resolved patterns. A resolved incident pattern may leave the gate only through a recorded superseding decision, so protection does not disappear when the original item closes.

message: Record current recurrence families for CI selection

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text:
Measured recurrence family, 2026-08-16 — "the check enumerates a set it maintains instead of the set the artifact defines". Scanned all 1,547 Issue and Task items, open and terminal.

Seven instances, six already fixed and one found today:

  pm-b84irw   closed   Measure source replication against an independently discovered denominator
  pm-te6elw   closed   SDK completeness asserted by a 10-case curated array against 85 declared actions
  pm-1jrdri   closed   The rendered command surface is not a subset of the contracted surface
  pm-6j7r1a   closed   The runtime contract enumeration is not closed over the surface it can resolve
  pm-xpumg4   closed   The boundary gate proves the CLI stopped importing private core and never proves it only imports the published SDK
  pm-7wx1f9   closed   Nested workspace snapshot and help paths are enumerated but not resolvable
  pm-suhxny   open     The public-surface gate enumerates its own hand-written entrypoint list; two published code exports ship ungoverned

Every one of them has the same three-part shape. A machine-readable artifact defines a set to the outside world — the export map, the workflow files, the command registration, the action table. A checker keeps its own enumeration of that set. The checker proves its list against the artifact and never proves the artifact against its list, so the check is complete over its own belief and silent about everything the artifact gained since the belief was written.

Two properties make this family worth detecting specifically rather than treating each instance as a one-off.

It fails open and it fails silently. Every one of the seven passed green while the gap existed. The failure is not a wrong answer, it is a correct answer to a smaller question, which is invisible in a pass/fail verdict and only appears when someone computes the denominator independently.

It recurs at the moment of growth. Nothing breaks when the hand list is written; the divergence begins the first time the artifact gains an entry. So the defect is introduced by a change that is unrelated to the checker, by an author who has no reason to look at it, which is precisely the situation review does not catch.

## The detectable signature

For pm-1qkivy this family is a concrete first target, because the signature is narrow enough to detect without drowning in false positives:

- a module under scripts/ or src/ that declares a frozen literal collection (Object.freeze over an object or array, or a `new Set([...])` of string literals), and
- reads a structured artifact in the same function or module — package.json, a workflows directory, a generated contract table, a registry JSON — and
- indexes into the artifact using members of the literal, rather than iterating the artifact.

That third clause is the discriminator. `for (const key of MY_LIST) lookup(artifact[key])` is the defect; `for (const key of Object.keys(artifact)) require(MY_MAP[key])` is the correct shape.

## The positive control already in the repository

scripts/release/gate-registry.mjs implements the correct shape. `discoverWorkflowGates` parses every file under .github/workflows and returns the real job identifiers, then `validateGateRegistry` checks both directions explicitly: `pipeline:<id>:unregistered` when the artifact has an entry the registry lacks, and `pipeline:<id>:not_enforced` when the registry has an entry the artifact lacks. The hand-maintained registry is annotation on a derived set, never the enumeration.

That gives any detector a same-repository positive control and a same-repository negative control, which is what pm-rtn5h6's escape ratchet asks every new gate to carry. It also means the fix for each instance is a known refactor rather than a design question.

## Cost of the escapes

Six shipped fixes for one shape. The seventh escaped into a published artifact: 2026.8.16 on npm resolves `@unbrained/pm-cli/cli` to a declaration file exporting 86 internal helpers, and the surface gate that exists to prevent exactly that reported "0 classified changes" for it. Installing the published tarball with bun and importing the entrypoint returns both symbols, typed.

Recorded on pm-1qkivy as a detector target and on pm-ouyq3n as a worked example of a recurrence the current relationship lexicon cannot express: these seven items are seven unrelated nodes to any graph walk, and the only thing tying them together today is this note.
